title: HC Kevin Stefanski & QB Michael Penix Jr. Post-game Press Conference | Week 6 | Falcons vs. Bears
text: Okay, starting uh on the injury front, Kendall Daniels is uh so far the reports are good. Uh he did have movement in his extremities uh out there on the field. Just I thought the the medical staff did outstanding job of of uh getting him to the uh to thank you getting him safely um off the field. Uh so all reports so far are good and we'll continue to pray that they remain good. Um, you know, that's a a disappointing one and I'm obviously proud of how we continue to fight, but to start like we started uh is really really disappointing and uh [clears throat] I just felt like we beat ourselves. They beat us. The the Bears beat us. Uh we also beat us and and that's really frustrating and that's something we we talk at length about and we talked at length about starting fast in this ball game and we did not. Uh really really that's uh on me and our and our staff. We got to get that fixed. Um because we we just put ourselves in the hole. So, uh disappointed. We'll have to look at, you know, h how we start and and make sure that we're putting our guys in position, but we'll own that one and and and we'll move on. But with that, I'll take any questions. >> Slow start obviously just why like what happened do you think there? Well, I think just offensively two three and outs both third downs if I'm not if I remember correctly were longer distances and it's just a tough place to live versus Dennis Allen and their defense. You got to give them credit, but uh we have to find a way to gain yards and score points early. >> Your pass game hit a pretty good rhythm there late, but opening three quarters is rough as well. Why couldn't it roll, do you think? I think all of the above, Daniel. Uh we just we need to do a better job installing a game plan. We got to do a better job of executing the game plan. All the above. Um but give them credit. >> Kevin, I was just curious what you uh spoke to with uh Zachariah Branch about after the the second fumble. >> Listen, Zachariah is somebody that we're going to be counting on. Uh he's a conscientious kid. He has to take care of the football. He has done a nice job up to date. He's a rookie. he will learn from this. But, uh, you turn the ball over three times versus a good team, it's going to be really, really hard to win. Uh, and obviously giving them field position where we gave them on on those plays, it's going to be even harder to win. So, uh, we're counting on him. He He's He'll be better for this. >> And if if I'm not mistaken, you guys practiced with some crowd noise this week in anticipation that you might deal with this. Is that correct? >> Yes. >> Were you on any sort of silent count? >> We were. Is is that frustrating for you at home? >> No. No. Listen, we we love our fans. Our fans are so supportive. Uh but we just felt like we knew that we'd likely need to be on the silent count. >> Uh coach, you talked about having the uh you know, the two long third downs to start the game. Um I think there was a third and two where Pendix had like a long five-step drop in early in the third quarter. Um were you happy with the play calling? >> I was. Yeah. And that particularly that play I thought we had a a a good play called versus the defense. We'll have to look at why we don't, you know, we need to get open there. We need to scheme them open. We need to work to get open. All all those things, but uh did not have an issue with that. No. >> Kevin, how would you describe Michael's play of the day and how healthy he is he right now? >> Yeah, I listen, Mike's healthy enough. Obviously, any time you're playing quarterback in this league, it's you're always going to feel the uh you know, this these defenses are good and all those things, but uh we just didn't play well enough as an offense for six 60 minutes. Uh obviously came on there and and fought like crazy and and made plays late. Uh but we have to look at ways to help this offense, help Mike gets get this offense going early. >> And what about Mike in particular? How well do you think he's he's played? Yeah, hard for me to say just coming on the heels of of of the game. Uh, but we just got to find ways to to score points, you know, we gota play we got to play way better early in the game. >> Kevin, only four carries for Bjan in the first half and nine overall. Do you wish you could have gotten the ball in his hands more during this game or is that part of the game? >> Yeah, of course. You know, that's game flow, etc. I I get that part, but uh we just that that's part of us needing to play way better early so that we can execute a game plan. >> Zachari tried to field the punt inside his 10. Do you have a particular rule about whether to do that or not or how >> ball that was fumbled, >> right? Yeah. >> Yes, we talk about it. There's a Yes, we have rules. Um there's also you have to know where the the punt team is relative to where you are if you have time, if you don't have time. So, we we'll continue to coach them. >> So, fair would rather not >> anytime you catch it inside the 10, you when you're doing that, you're assuming that they're not down there already. Uh, and you feel like you have a return. So, we'll look at it. >> You went for it a couple times on fourth down. How much of it had to do with like the lead, you know, trying to come back and how much of it had to do with Ben Johnson's just aggressiveness, you know, highscoring offense? I think anytime you make those decisions, it's always uh dependent on the where you are in the game, what the distance is, what play call you have, and then obviously late in the game, we're we're four down as as the drive starts because we we need multiple scores. So, uh you I'll always make those decisions what you feel like you need for that particular moment. fourth quarter was where really where the offense started kind of coming to a little bit. Um able to get two drives, two two-point conversions. What did you see that you really liked on those two drives? >> Yeah, obviously the uh pass protection was good. We got the ball out. We made big play. We made explosive plays uh in in those moments and then to come through on those two-point plays obviously is huge when you're down by 24. So, uh, I thought the guys executed well, understood the situation that we were in, uh, but obviously not enough and and truly we just have to be better early in the game, uh, is really the answer >> there. Uh, defensive back number six, Gordon, got gave you guys some trouble in the pass rush. >> Did was that just scheme or not accounting for him? How do you >> Yeah, he's an excellent blitzer. We knew that going into this game. Uh, Dennis Allen does a very good job with his blitz looks. uh we have to look at everything and say, you know, are we giving our guys the best plan to to block those type of guys and have answers in those things. So, you got to tip your cap to them and then we'll look at what we can do better. >> Kevin, what do you think appeared to lead to some of their success in the screen game? It seems like they had a lot of guys in space when they were getting to the left and right side of the lines. >> Yeah, it's a difficult uh it's a difficult scheme to defend. uh they they challenge you in a bunch of different ways the way they they run it and the way they throw it and the screens are a huge part of what they do and they do them from all personnel groupings on all down distances. So obviously that's something that we worked on this week and a lot of it is is simply running to the football and uh again if they made plays we got to just look at ways that we we can defend them better but it's it's definitely a big part of what they do. >> Kevin, could you talk about just how you were addressing the team and coaching the team during Kendall's injury? Obviously, it kind of creates a delay in the game, and I'm just kind of curious how you get >> Listen, those are those are those are no fun for anybody. Uh players, coaches, uh you don't want to see anyone down like that. And Kendall's a kid that we all love, we all respect. Um now, and then you got to play football and and that's the hard part. It's easy for me to say, but uh you got to play. Um, now they take comfort in knowing that he's doing better. But, uh, yeah, in those moments, those are hard because all you're thinking about is is this young man that you know and you love and and you want to make sure he's okay. Um, and then what you want to do once he's you feel like he's safe now, you got to go out there, you got to coach, and you got to go play. >> You're 0 and three at home. There's nothing you can do about it now, obviously, but imagine that feels like an opportunity lost. >> Yeah, you have to shoot. You got to win your games at home and uh it's very very disappointing. Uh you know, this is a place that we love to play and and we love to play in front of our fans and and not to be able to to win this one uh stings and and we got to find ways uh to play better and coach better and and starting this week. >> What are the ways to start getting into the win column, especially in a division that is still up for grabs as of now? >> Sure. Uh, you know, in this game, we turned it over three times. Uh, I think we're 0 for three on fourth down. Hard to do versus a good football team. So, we got to make sure that we're not beating ourselves, and that'll be a good place to start. >> Okay. Thank you guys. [music] >> What's up, Mike? The way you guys passed the ball early on was was slow and rough. Obviously, you kind of hit a pretty good stride there late. What do you think flipped from, I guess, third quarter onward, I guess, like >> in your >> Yeah. Um, you know, first of all, I want to thank God, you know, uh, you know, just getting us all out healthy, you know, praying for Kendall. Obviously, uh, he he had an injury, but, you know, he's he got every like we're we're good. Um, he's going to be good. And uh I also want to talk about just uh obviously we see a lot of people wearing pink as well. So I want to hit on that like just um praying for all the families that you know has to go go through you know the breast cancer. You know obviously this is awareness month so you know definitely don't want to um you know just go look over that because that's just something that you know a lot of people a lot of families have been affected um over and you know just praying for for those people. But, uh, to answer your question, um, I'll just say we just started executing better. Started executing better early on. We we were slow like you said, you know, um, just wasn't executing whenever the the play was there. And, you know, obviously the the scoreboard early on showed that. >> You guys had to practice this week with crowd noise, right? How early on did you guys run silent count and and kind of [clears throat] how often today? >> Um, oh, we we did silent count all week, so we were good with the silent count stuff. Um, crowd noise thing, you know. Uh it's it's always tough, you know, whenever you're playing home and you know, you hear early in the week, it's like uh we might got to work silent cadence cuz you know, you always expect, you know, uh our fans overrule um you know, the opponent's fans, but we we were ready for it and um I feel like we executed a silence cadence well. So, >> Michael, how well do you think you're progressing right now as an NFL quarterback? Are you pleased with where you are right now? >> Uh you never please. You know, you know, it's always work to do. There's always ways to get better and that's what I'm trying to do each and every day, you know, figure that out. I'm going to go to the drawing board, see what we did uh this game and, you know, try to figure out how I can be better for this team to help us win a football game. So, I never say I'm pleased. You know, we still got work to do. >> And what about healthwise? How do you feel right now? >> Yeah, I feel good health-wise. I feel good. Um, yep. My ribs, I I came out of the game last week for that. You know, those held up and, you know, I feel good. Mike Kevin said that slow starts something you had already talked about. What do you need to do from your perspective to get going faster as an offense? >> We just got to come ready to play and we got to execute. You got to execute like like I kind of hinted on. We just got to execute the simple things, you know. Uh we we always have a great game game plan. you know, these first couple weeks, I've I've always, you know, uh loved the game plan that we had in and we all felt com confident and comfortable with, you know, everything that was on the play play sheet and um we knew what to expect. It's not like they went out there and did any uh too many things that surprised us, you know, so you know, for us as a offense, you know, we got to go out and execute at a high level and, you know, not not start slow and like with what you're saying, you we got to figure out a way to start fast. >> You you got hit a bunch today. You said you you feel good. Does does it feel good to go through a game like that and feel good if I'm ask if I'm >> Do it feel good to go through a game where I got hit a bunch >> and and but but come out of it healthy and feel like you're >> Yeah, I mean it's football, you know. I go in expecting you you know I'm going to get hit at some point, you know. It's a football game, you know, we're playing good teams, you know, uh and not just saying like sackwise, but I could run, I can scramble. So, it's so many ways, you know, uh it's hard to avoid contact, you know. It's it's no avoiding contact in this sport, you know. But it it does feel good to, you know, come out healthy, you know. So that's something that, you know, obviously in my past, you know, I wasn't doing a lot, but to every game I don't take it for granted. Every time I come out healthy, like I come up here, I say, "Thank God, you know, uh, for the health and, you know, um, I just want to keep playing ball." >> So I'm over here, but um, what has been the biggest difference in your eyes between playing at home versus on the road? I know you talked a little bit about crowd noise, silent count, stuff like that. So, what has been the diff biggest difference for you? >> What do you mean? >> Like playing on the road versus playing at home? Like >> what's the biggest difference? >> Like I'm saying from like a success perspective. Like cuz you guys have, you know, got two road games >> because we won two road games, lost two home games. >> Basically, >> it's no difference. It's football. We got to come out to play. We got to come out, execute. No matter where we playing at, we got to find a way to win. That's that's all it is. Mike, can can you just kind of take us through um your your what you were doing with the guys when Kendall was down when you had that delay in the game? Did at some point you got to get the guys together to kind of get minds right or just take us through that situation from your perspective? >> Yeah, I mean everybody went out on the field, you know, uh you know, just you know, just told him that, you know, we're we're there for him and uh we just pray for him. You know, that's that's all we could do at at that moment. We don't know what's going on with him. um we saw he was moving so that was obviously a positive and that was something that you know uh give us hope you know but uh all you can do is pray for him in that moment and you know just be there for him as a teammate. So >> were you able to communicate with him while he was down or was he communicating with anybody at all? >> Yeah he he said he said y'all go he's like y'all go finish this off. That's what he said when he was uh getting carded off. He said y'all go finish this off. So you know he was in good good spirits. uh when you guys fall in a hole 14 nothing 21-7 how much does that take Bejian out of the game and the running game out of the game one of your one of your top weapons like how difficult does it become when you're when you're fighting uphill >> I mean it's it's always tough you know uh being down that much you know like like we talked about you know starting fast is something that you always want to do but you know uh sometimes you get in obvious passing situations you know and obviously you know whenever you're doing that you know the defense they they their mindset is just defend a pass, you know, so they're not thinking about defending the run. So, uh, for us, we just can't get, uh, off a schedule like that. We got to find a way to start fast so that, you know, we can't keep bean in the game. We can't keep, you know, the running backs and the running game going, uh, so that we can go out there and execute things in the pass game as well. >> Throughout your career, there's been a lot of noise about the quarterback room, your health situation. going forward, what are the things that you need to focus on specifically to continue, you know, staying in and staying healthy and also improving your skills? >> Um, just keep doing what I'm doing, you know, trusting God, you know, uh, preparing at a high level, you know, making sure I'm taking care of my body, you know, um, whether that's in the training room, you know, at home, you know, whenever I'm doing stuff, you know, my diet, stuff like that. But, you know, you just got to take care of yourself as a as a person. So, >> I have a couple couple more injury things for a person that's been injured as much as you. you seem to handle it extremely well as far you don't seem to be dwelling on the past or or anything that's happened in the past. Is that true number one? And number two, I know you went into the injury tent at one point. Uh what was that all about? >> Yeah. Um I don't think about it, you know. Uh I I have I have uh strong faith, you know. I trust in God. You know, obviously uh you always hear the saying God, you know, he give his toughest battles to his strongest soldiers. And um you know, I just kind of let that stick with me and I just continue to go out there and just have fun and keep doing what I love. I did go into the injury tent. I'm not going to say what that was about. Um but I was good. Just know I was good. >> Question about Kyle, you know, what was it that was going to him? A lot of people wanted to say, "Well, he goes to Drake, but he doesn't go to Kyle." Seems like you guys really had something in the fourth quarter. What was it? just he was open or or just what? yeah, we just playing ball. You know, for me, um my job is to execute the plays that's called and uh find a find an open guy and also and obviously, you know, whenever KP is open, I'm not just looking past them, you know. So, uh that whole narrative is crazy, you know, especially with him being the person I spent the most of my time with since I've been here, you know. So, for people to say, "Oh, I don't think about Kyle. I only think about Drake." It's like it's somebody I was with every day in the offseason like what are we talking about you know but um you know we just playing the game you know um obviously like I said from from the f first week back is like we want to get him the ball you know obviously he's one of our our best players on the team so we got to get all our best players opportunity to go be great and uh we're going to continue to do that >> else. Thank y'all. All >> [music] >> right.

title: Panthers vs. Eagles Week 6 Postgame Reaction | Carolina Panthers
text: They don't ask you how it looked, they ask you how you did. And the Panthers did it right. They come up with a 2514 win over the Philadelphia Eagles to go to three and two on the year and to now have a game and a half lead in the NFC South along with Eugene Robinson, Mike Pico, Brett McBillan. Hey, glad to have you with us here on the Panthers postgame show brought to you by Marcos Pizza. The Panthers pulled it out. The Eagles are banged up. We know that the Panthers are banged up. And Eugene, you've said it for years. Nobody feels sorry for anybody else in the National Football League. >> You're absolutely right. Nobody feels sorry for you. Yeah. Here it is. Uh the Carolina Panthers. I mean, you go into a hostile environment. You know that everybody's down. You know that there's no Saquon Barkley. You find out early in the week that oh man, their guy Jaylen Herz is out of the mix. And so you're expecting to go ahead and not only win the game, but win the game, you know, maybe convincingly. And that wasn't the case. And I think it was a really tough game in the first half and it looked like we just couldn't get get our footing and and I'm happy for the win. No doubt about that. But I'm I'm cautious because it was too many penalties and that's going to that's going to bite you. That's going to catch up with you. It's going it just always does. And so there's got to be a lot of things that you have to eliminate. So I know that when coach Canales when he addresses a team, he's going to go ahead and mention, hey, we got to clean some things up. We got to clean some things up. However, taking advantage of a team like this and winning on the road, that's a big big plus as you come back home to Baker America Stadium. >> Well, and Mike, you and I talked about it this past week on our on our podcast about the fact that >> if you could have gotten the Eagles down by a couple touchdowns early, this is the kind of crowd that that would I mean, three losses in a row for the Eagles. That's the kind of crowd that turns against you. >> Oh, absolutely. Absolutely. >> Yeah, I think it's Mike. [laughter] >> Absolutely. Yeah. Absolutely. >> Do your Do you spike your cheeks? >> You can shout real loud. [laughter] >> I know. I think your microphone was a little There we go. There we go. There we go. There we go. There we go. All right. Now we're back. Now we're back. >> I you know it was to your point, right? It was maybe the numbers didn't from the scoring perspective weren't where they wanted to be. But when you look at when we I know we'll do the stats a little bit later, but the overall numbers I mean 399 total yards to 222 Gan. And so it was um to your point about it it's it's how many how many wins not how much you win by right so the the win was the important piece and it you know this is you know I the old cliche I mean Eagles get paid too even though they had a bunch of bunch of injuries but it was a it was a case where Panthers were dominant and when it was uh when the game was in the balance they made some big plays >> you know you talked about Brett about how this this that audience could actually turn against you >> there was a situation where before Chipper Chuba Huber makes that that touchdown in the second half. It was a fourth down and one and Bryce Young was able to go ahead and do a hard count down there and the defense jumped off sides. >> Typically, you can't even hear. You wouldn't be able to hear because all the the team would be going the the fans would be going crazy screaming, trying to make as much noise as possible just to get a false start. But that wasn't the case. He was able to go, you know, sit and everybody jumped off the off sides. I'm going that tells you that the Panthers had quieted that crowd uh and and got them to a minimum of like of applause and so and that's really kind of unheard of. So I got to give the Carolina Panthers a lot of credit because you go into a hostile environment and you hush the crowd. >> Well, and you knew going into the game that yes, the Eagles offense was banged up and the Eagles offense is going to struggle and you had opportunities to really shut them down, >> but the Eagles defense is pretty healthy. >> You know that's right. and they're pretty good. And you know, you had some good field position early in the game >> and still were only putting three points on the board. And I always feel uncomfortable when you're down when you're leading by a score or less because one freak play can turn things around and all of a sudden you're behind. >> And Ch here it is in that first half to Brett's point. Uh there was third down situations, but it was third and 10, third and 12, third and 15, third and 21. It was like almost impossible situations. Our third down percentage in the first half had to be close to nil. It had to be one for six. >> I know. So we end up being seven for 17, but one for six, it was wful. And the distance to go ahead and try to go ahead and get third and 12 that those those distances are hard to get. you know, third and 12, third and 18, third and 21, third and 10. You want to keep things manageable. Third and three, third and four, third and five, third and two, third and one. That's those are manageable dis uh distance that you can go ahead and capitalize on. Typically, you don't have a a play for third down and 21. I mean, even when you pick it up by Jaylen Coker, that's still not a play that you that you designed to have. You can't you can't expect that. >> You can't expect that. You can't expect that. So, that was another thing that I thought that you got to give Philadelphia credit. Their defense was explosive. They did a great job of stacking the box, taking away the run uh first, getting pressure on on Bryce and keeping us in positions where either we were holding and there was a penalty called or that there was a long distance of third down to go ahead and try to cover and we couldn't get it done. >> Yeah. And give credit too to the Eagles offense. I mean early in the third quarter when they ste started to speed up a little bit. >> Yes. You know, that helped. you helped and they they were able to get the touchdown drive, the second touchdown of the game and then then things got a little bit close. >> Yeah, it did. But then you did you see how uh coach Gerald he flipped the switch? He started becoming much more of aggressive and started uh you stacking that box and blitzing and getting in the face of of that young quarterback. That I thought was definitely what you needed to have happen because when we were sitting back in the zone letting them catch the ball in front and said come up make the tackle. It's not the same mentality and I've been there. It's not the same mentality. You know, you worry whether your secondary can hold up. Well, Will Lee showed me a lot today. He showed me >> they picked on him too. I mean, they went after him a lot. >> He showed me that he's he's one of the better corners in the league. He he he was covering. He covered extremely well. Even on a touchdown against Smith, on that test outdown on the on the right hand side, he almost punched that ball out and that was a wellplaced thrown ball by the quarterback. And so, I mean, I got to give the defense a lot of lot of credit. And I tell you what, Will Lee, you showed me that you're that guy. You're definitely that guy. >> Yeah. And you got to clean up the penalties. I mean, clean it up. >> It was 14 in the both teams had 14 penalties in the first half. Panthers had eight. And not that there's ever a good time for a penalty, but it was that they all came after uh what three of them came off on on punt returns. Special two I think after good punt returns. >> Incom I think had that uh yeah I think he had >> after good punt returns it cost you a lot of field position. I mean I don't think you know the numbers you were looking at in the first half. I mean the Panthers had eight penalties for 105 yards in the first half. >> Three of those came on punt returns. And I don't think that accurately reflects how much because you're penalized from the spot of the foul, >> not from where the runner ended up ended up. Exactly. And here it is. I I thought that having uh HN back in the game at that he [clears throat] was a spark today. He was an incredible special team spark. No doubt about that. I thought he did a a wonderful job of not only catching the ball, but also getting up the field and getting some positive yards. This was the first time I thought our our special teams, maybe the first time that you noticed the the the offense of the run game, you notice it more like, hey, we're picking up, you know, 15 yards head. Oh, that's a 30 yard run, man. You know, that's bolds well as you move forward. And I thought that he did a great job. >> And the average start for the Panthers was their own 31. And for the Eagles, it was their own 21. >> Wow. Big big difference. That's a big difference. >> That's even including the penalty, >> right? It's with the penalties. Think how much better it would have been if you take the three penalties off. >> Take the penalties off the table. >> But I do want to talk about one special teams play that I thought was a crucial moment of the game because in fact it is our what a burger. What a moment of the game. Grilling delicious food for 75 years. What a burger. Just like you like it. >> Prevents a pass interference. The blocked high up into the air. It goes forward and the Panthers let it roll out of bounds at the 49 yd line of Philadelphia. Carolina blocks the punt. >> I thought this sequence was huge. >> Yes, >> because the Pan, you know, the Eagles had just scored to make it 1914. The Panthers went three and out >> and the Eagles had the ball at their own >> 48 yardd line and then the snap goes through McKe's legs for a 12 yd loss. >> Then you then the Panthers get called for pass interference and they go, "Oh, no, no, no. Eric Brown tipped the ball which negates the pass interference >> blocked punt and then that gives the Panthers the ball at the 48 yd line at the Eagles 48 yd line and then four plays later they're in the end zone 2514. All of that cons just barreled barrel rolled and it just completely changed the momentum of the game >> and that's what I'm sorry and that's what coach Canales is looking for as far as a special teams play. You're always looking for a special team spark. It's my coach co coaches used to always say it's 23% of the game or it's 25% of the game. It's 28% of the game. They those plays absolutely matter. And when you get a a run or you get a a punch out for a fumble or you get here in this case a a block punt, those are huge plays and you can see it on the sideline. Guys are going crazy. They're absolutely going crazy. And what does it do on the other side? It demoralizes the Philadelphia Eagles like, "Oh, what else can happen? They already got people falling down and getting hurt. So now what else can happen?" Well, guess what? They blocked it and now they put four plays later in the end zone. >> And it doesn't count as a turnover, but it has kind of the same effect from a momentum standpoint for the Panthers because they they basically there was no no gain on that drive. I mean, they essentially where they started. >> It was a nineyard punt. A nineyard punt. and and then you got the ball on the plus side of the the field so you don't have that, you know, that far to go. And now you're looking at, hey, I can go ahead and get a field goal and still put this game out of reach. >> Yeah. And exactly at that, you know, right at the time you thought the Eagles, you were worried the Eagles had taken the moment of this game. All they had to do was go down, score a touchdown, and I mean, there's still over nine, you know, nine minutes to go in the game. 8 I mean, that came with 8:24. That was at 8:24. So there's still nine minutes to go in the game when the Eagles got the ball back and you were worried they could still go down, score a touchdown and take the lead. >> But that was the beauty of coach Agerro because that's when he got aggressive and said, "Look, I'm not sitting back in any zone. I'm putting my guys in in your face." And they came after him. >> Bryce Young today, gentlemen, 20 of 39, 289 yards, and two touchdowns. He also rushed three times for six yards. Uh, but I want to talk about the fact that I thought even though these aren't the numbers we've seen from him in other games so far this year, I thought his decision making was still spot on. I thought some, you know, a couple times we had to scramble out of the pocket or had to get rid of the ball quickly. even throwing the ball away. And >> this game allows you to do that even more. >> Yeah, I mean, I think after the by-week I felt just better physically just in general, just just getting out there and trusting myself and running and um just just being who I am, you know? I mean just being able to be available and be ready. I thought I mean kind of in training camp and to the end of training camp into the regular season that V did a great job bringing in a lot of competition and so guys are ready to step up when their number is called and so um with that as well as how we run the ball and and how we we've been protecting we've been able to keep the offense going and then the hope is that we obviously be able to to continue to hope the hope is that we also be able to continue to build on that and that we can be available and that we can be 8 n deep on the offensive line need 10 and guys that we trust that can go in there and Yeah, >> we're losing hands. Go ahead. >> You know, as Nate's question, let's just follow up on that. Just to have someone like Ready, even though he's not playing right now, you know, to be in those lists prepared and then be even. Does that give you just a little bit of motivation knowing that you're chasing the best? >> It does give you motivation, but it's still so far away. And there's so many games I have more I have to win and and Super Bowls and all that different type of stuff. All I can focus on is today and and winning today and then moving on to the Seahawks next week. And um I mean he's got like 50 more years. Like I'm only 30. I'm 31. He's played to 45. So it's that's a long ways away, but like I said, it's always an honor to to to be in a any conversation um with him um and the way he played the game cuz that's how you want to play it. You want to be a competitor. You want to win and you want to bring your teammates along. And that that's who I want to be as my career goes on. >> Thanks Patrick. Tight wing left, three receivers. But um we're just going to continue to build. We have a lot of youth, a lot of good vets and our football's complimentary. Like your secondary making plays makes it better for us. Your defense align making plays makes it better for your secondary. So we just going to continue to pick ping pong off each other and just keep building. >> And the fact that you have to be so versatile. We saw you in a standup role here again today. I thought he's going to get another pick like last year. Uh but the different things you're asked to do in executing the scheme. >> Um obviously I just trust bags man. They be calling me to do a little bit more uh different things move around just so we can get more players on the field more Dline. Uh it's obviously I think it's genuinely a blessing just to be trusted in that way. Uh it's a lot but uh they they put on me because they they have faith that I can handle it and I have faith that I can perform to their what their standard is. So, um, it just I don't know. It's just I'm I'm thankful for it. >> Well, Ashley, I want to ask you too because in defense like a sudden change like they muff punt, they get the ball and now out the 40 yardd line or they get the 57 yd pass to the one and you guys go not getting in. I'm asking about mindset here and a mentality of a defense of saying, "Uh-uh, that's not going to happen." Yeah, we our our mindset every week is basically to defend every blade of grass. Like, as long as we have a place to stand, we have somewhere to fight for them. And that's our mentality and that's how we try to carry ourselves in pride and always swarm to the ball, hunt as a pack and you know do do what we do to to stop teams. And I mean that that was a display of it. >> Final question. It's not just your sack but three other sacks in this game but we felt like hitting line drives right at somebody in baseball. You know it was coming. What was the key today to finish and complete those plays? >> It's just uh the same thing. It's just what it's always been. It's always been effort and just being relentless to the ball. We got rushers who can win. It's sometimes it's just circumstance. It's the right time, the right moment. So, uh we just got to make the make the sacks when we can. >> You guys get a safety. Sure looked like it. >> I thought it was a safety, but you know, I I can't argue with officials just like I can't argue about roughing the passers, but >> Okay, we'll just leave it. Let that go. But what we know, one full sack. A full sack for Ashton Gelati. >> Mhm. Yeah. Uh the 33 yder, it was pretty open, you know. Uh Jake came across and kicked out and it was just a lane and uh kind of bent the angle and then I scored that one. Um what was the other one? I don't even know that one. >> Second touchdown bounce off. >> Oh yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. 36. So it was going right but uh I seen the left was open and you know Pat came down and made a block and you know I just dove over the defender. >> Is there moments on plays like that where you're not even sure you're going to get out of it? Um >> yeah, of course. You know, um usually I'm just trying to get back to the line of scrimmage if something break down, but uh uh obviously it was open backside and we made it work. >> What you think of the blocking ability of the team? >> What' you say? >> What you see the blocking ability of the team? >> Uh yeah. Yeah, he did he always do great, you know, even in training camp. Uh he he usually see the cut back before I do and then he go down and block the guy, you know. Uh that's real unselfish. This is probably the best start you could have imagined, Ken, through five weeks. Is it >> more surprising to you than even what you may have wanted or expected when you joined the Chiefs? >> Uh, nah, it's not surprising, you know, um, you know, like we've been going through it during training camp at OTA. So, um, that's kind of what you you expect, you know, the way these guys work up front and uh, making my job and image shop a lot easier. So, um, I just we just just got to continue to go and execute. >> I remember you saying that you wanted to join us because you felt like Andy and Eric and Marshall could make you better >> through these five games. Are there ways that you can see one better at this than even a year ago? >> Um yeah, and just um just me personally, I always want to get better uh each as years go on, you know, you want to uh learn stuff. So, um definitely, you know, having those guys in my corner makes it a lot easier. Xavier was saying that opposing defenders sometimes can tell him like, "Oh, K9's different." Like, do you ever hear that when you're on the field and what's your reaction to? >> Yeah. Um, you know, after the game it's like a lot of a lot of respect, like mutual respect even in the game, you know, so um it's cool, you know, cuz guys that you play against feel like you're a baller. So, uh it's cool to see around the league. >> Have you heard this next game circle? Is this going to be different for you to go be going back to Seattle on the other side? >> Um, yeah. Right now I'm just focused on, you know, uh, we got to go critique the mistakes that we made and then, you know, once we get to that that point, we'll see. >> You're on a I mean, you guys have won five games in a row, but when you were with Seattle, you had won your last 10 maybe. >> Been a long time since you lost the game. What that's like? >> Um, I really don't speak on that, you know. Um, yeah, that's it. on that first touchdown, did you look on the video board and kind of adjust to on the angle because it looked like some guys had an angle on you? >> Yeah. No, I didn't. Uh I knew since I end up stumbling through the hole, uh I knew somebody was chasing, so I looked to my left and that was the closest one. So, I kind of bent the angle so it'll be harder for him to catch me. >> Where do you think the offense is? Just uh if you had to kind of evaluate them, is this just the beginning of what we'll see throughout the season? >> Yeah, definitely. I feel like uh we're going to get better. you know, we got a lot of stuff we got to execute and get better at and more detailed at, including myself, but you know, um, we just going to continue to get better. >> You mentioned critiquing. >> Mhm. >> I mean, you 19 points at halftime, you got the two touchdowns, but only three points in the second half. So, you know, I mean, what do you attribute that to? What was Andy's message about, you talked about finish, but about finishing the game. Yeah, it was really uh EB came and talked to us, you know, how intense he is and, you know, um really just talked about executing and uh doing better when we um get the opportunities like the goal line and stuff like that. So, um really just got to execute better and be more detailed in our work. >> Kenneth, you talked about executing better. I know coach Reed said that he wanted to get better like in the short yardage game. Is that something you take pride in? >> Yeah, definitely. Um as a runner, you always want to get that one yard, you know? Um and yeah, that's pretty much how I look at it. We just got to get that one yard no matter what. >> On fourth and one, are you are you pleading your case? You know, like let's let's go for it. >> Yeah. Yeah, definitely. I always want to go for it. >> Thank you everybody. Thank you. >> The Chiefs get the victory 22 to6 over the Chargers. Chiefs are 5-0. People are excited here in the locker room club and the Chargers are only six. Only the fifth team in NFL history to start this way after having 11 plus wins the season prior. But defensively in the second half, it became fun. There were takeaways in this game. Fumble, great play uh with Drew Tranle the fumble recovery, Nick Bolton separating the receiver from the ball, but then also to get fourth down stops and four sacks. I finally blew the dust on radio off the McDonald's card because it had been sitting there in dust for six weeks, but to get four to match the season total was pretty good. >> And we were so close over the last three games. I mean, in that Raiders game, they were pressuring Cousins throughout the game. It couldn't get him to the ground. Kind of felt that happening early in this game. And Herbert's a big guy, hard to take to the ground, but finally we saw the sacks start to come later on in the game. For George, it felt like a frustration sack. Like finally, there we go. He had like a thousand pressures before that. But uh yeah, great to see the four sacks here in this one. We held the Chargers out of the end zone. That's obviously the most important number of the day. But really to me, whenever it seemed like the Chargers were building momentum, our defense came up and made a play. Whether it was the interception, the fumble recovery, a fourth down stop, a pass breakup, something. Whenever the Chargers had some momentum building, our defense said, "No, not today." And that was a great thing to see. The defense really won this game here today. >> Yeah. And no bigger situation than after a muff punt u by Nico Roiho, the Chiefs are going to get the ball at the plus 40. He fumbles it. Chargers get it back after a challenge. The defense said, "No, that's it. We're going to stuff you and knock it down." When you look at the Chargers offense, it came down to 57 yards on one play to Quenton Johnson, and that's pretty much it. Yeah, otherwise the Chiefs defense stuffed these guys all day. Great against the run. They did not let the Charger run game get going. And Vidal, we know he's a he's a threat. We know Hampton's a threat. Mitchell's a threat, but the Chiefs didn't let the running game get going. >> No, they didn't. And here's the deal. I mean, the Chiefs left a lot of points on the board here today. Uh offensively, we outgainained the Chargers 422 to 259. The issue was we were one for four in the red zone in terms of touchdown efficiency, and two red zone trips didn't score any points at all. So, why do I say all this? Well, the defense picked up the offense here in this game. The offense had an opportunity to put this game away. They didn't do it, but the defense time and time again whenever the Chargers had some momentum building said, "Don't worry, we got this." And we saw it there throughout the game and particularly at the very end. >> Did Phoenix have a safety on that? >> I think he did, but you know what? Oh well. I've never seen a football that backed up before in my life. It was like an index card. That was crazy. >> Really close. Uh, some things, some milestones here before we close. Patrick Mahomes now has 100 career wins in the regular season. He's done that in 131 games. That ties Tom Brady for the fastest mark to 100 uh career regular season wins in NFL history. That's big. >> We can't take him for granted. I mean, just incredible. This is our experience as Chiefs fans. We essentially have Tom Brady as our quarterback and his name is Patrick Mahomes. And you know, I have not forgotten about December the 14th, the last time we saw these guys. That was a really tough day in Chief's Kingdom. We lose that game. Uh we were eliminated from the playoffs and Patrick has lost for the season. Terrace's ACL. To think about the things that have happened since then. I'm feeling pretty good here today. We're 5-0 playing these guys now. They're 0 and six. We're going in the right direction and they're not. >> What do I think about the Spongebob post? >> Yeah, no Spongebob posts, I don't think, for the Chargers after this one. >> You kind of got me fired up for this game when you reminded me of that. Here's the other milestone. It's big. The Chiefs now start 5-0. It's the third time that Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes together have started 5-0. That joins a very select group in NFL history. Oh, Bill Bichc, Tom Brady. Oh, Pton Manning and Tony Dunie. And oh, going back to Vikings times, Bud Grant and Fran Tarkington. So, that put gives it in perspective of what the Chiefs have done with this head coach and this quarterback. >> Just incredible. And you mentioned the word perspective. I think last year added a lot of perspective for all of us where we were two and three through five games last year. To be 5-0, to have everything out in front of us, to be 3 and 0 in the division. You can't take it for granted because last year showed how hard these games really are. So happy for our guys, happy to be 5-0. Let's get after the Seahawks next week. One final thing I said as I closed out the radio broadcast, gird your loins, >> get your chin strapped, pack your backpack. Six of the next eight on the road. >> Yeah. And three of those are on prime time and we're going to be flip-flopping the country. Going to get tough, but the Chiefs are going to go into this stretch at 5-0. >> Yeah, it won't be easy. Always difficult playing football on the road, but yeah, it's a lot easier when you're 5-0 playing winning football and feeling pretty good. Let's get after these guys next week. >> Chiefs win at 22 to6. 5-0. Chargers are 0 and6 for Matt McMullen. I'm Mitch Holtus. Gard your loins and get ready for the road ahead. title: Indianapolis Colts fall to Tennessee Titans 26-20, fall to 2-4
text: Joel, I've been on this beat now for just about 365 days. So, I don't have a whole lot to go off of. You've been on doing this for much, much longer. Is this the worst Colts loss that you have experienced in your time in Indianapolis? >> I I It's hard to say the worst because there was obviously the the dark depths of the Jeff Saturday interim appearance where they give up the NFL's biggest lead. I think in terms of when this team still has a chance, it's one of the worst that I can remember. Because even in that 2022 season, the they were actually fairly competitive up until they benched Matt Ryan uh in that season. That their losses that season were to teams that ended up in the playoffs. Um they didn't look good, like this team didn't look good, but they didn't lose to a team that was 0-5 in the way they lost today. It feels like the final straw. I I don't know what that means for when. I don't know what Carl Ursery Gordon is thinking on that. We don't have it. But it just it feels like the final straw for this regime barring some miraculous comeback against Minnesota and Jacksonville and Dallas. >> In case you had a way to miss it, the Colts lose this one 26 to 20 at Lucas Oil Stadium as Joel mentioned um to a previously winless 0-5 Titans team that we mentioned on the podcast this week. Um I think we'd even mentioned in stories was a team that I think was better than their record had suggested. Most of those losses had been one-score games. They'd played um pretty tough competition. And this this did not feel like the same um rudderless Titans team that came into last season that got their doors blown off. Um gave up some big Jonathan Taylor runs and um just didn't didn't really have any answers. This This Titans team, although same time was down 0 to 13, 13 to 0 going into the locker room, this game felt like it was um an uninspiring win that the Colts had in hand and yet they found ways in the second half to lose it. They gave up 20 straight points. Um lose in an in a game where they on the offensive side of the ball had 399 yet net yards only give up 186. not many teams find ways to lose and yet the Colts did today. >> Yeah, I I thought, you know, going off of what you said about about the Titans, I thought they looked even worse than their reputation or what we've been led to believe based on some of those those closer scores they played. They They They The one thing that they supposedly could do well was stop the run. They didn't stop the run today. Uh the Colts just gave the handed them the game. >> Daniel Jones handed them the game. That gamble has not paid off at all that he's could be the guy he was in the first before the injury last season. I don't even think it's the injury. That's the thing. I think that's the most troubling thing to me. I think blaming it on the Achilles at this point is a mistake. The mistakes are They're not about the Achilles. You You throw an interception aiming for Will Mallory when you have Seth McGowan wide open in the flat. That has nothing to do with your Achilles tendon. Like that pass wasn't open. It's not an arm strength thing. That's a decision-making thing. And last year at this point in the season we were talking about how good his decision-making was. His decision-making has been terrible. He's been awful against the blitz. Gus Bradley traditionally does not blitz. They dialed some stuff up today. Six sacks for the Titans. And that's some of that's on the quarterback. It just is. Maybe a lot of it's on the quarterback when when you come down to it. He just He just has not been what they need to be. He He gave the game away. They They struggled. Brian Mason who's typically been good really lost a match-up with a much more experienced coordinator today in the punt game. Um but really just a shocking loss given how bad this Titans team is. They They had 186 total yards. You have to win a game that you give up 186 total yards. That's Colts had more than that by halftime. >> And to end in a divisional game at home and to a previously winless Titans team. As you mentioned, this is coming into this game the Titans and the Colts both had two turnovers. Titans managed to get three turnovers today on the Colts. Two of them by two of them really bad really one bad interception from Daniel Jones, one on a tipped ball that I think you can lay on the shoulders of Josh Downs who had a really rough game today with three drops. Another really tough fumble from Jonathan Taylor similar to the one that we saw from him a couple weeks ago in week one here against the Ravens in Lucas Oil Stadium. And this was also as you mentioned a Titans team that got six six sacks today. They only had 10 sacks coming into this game. This is not you know, when I say that this Titans team was maybe a little bit better than the record or at least the the scores that they'd put up early in the season suggested that there were lots of weak points in this team and yet they really kind of flipped the script on this Colts team in the second half and now the trick is the Colts have to find a way to turn this around going to a defense that is I mean if this if they had a tough time with this defense I don't know what you can expect to see on Sunday >> against Brian Flores in Minnesota. >> It It like I said it it feels like the end. It feels like the beginning of the end the end the end. I Like I said I don't know what Carl Irsay Gordon does. I don't know what her plan is. I It's just really hard to see this team coming back from this at this point. And I I I think you could see it in the reactions. I I don't think I've ever seen Shane Steichen that emotional clearly very clearly livid at the end of the game. The Force Buckner very upset. Jonathan Taylor very upset. It's just hard to hard to see how they come back from this. >> We will have a lot more on all those emotions those reactions how this game was lost on indystar.com. Be sure to tune in for the Colts Cover 2 podcast. We'll be taping that tonight. We'll have that probably for you early tomorrow morning for your drive to work or whenever you get a chance to listen to it. Check that out on whatever pod podcast platform you please. We'll have videos from the locker room Shane Steichen's reaction Daniel Jones on our Colts YouTube channel. Check all of that out and more on indystar.com. He's Joel A. Erickson. I'm Nathan Brown. >> First win of the season. Yeah. How do you explain this one? >> Um it hurts. We can't We just can't do that. The fact that we just gave them this win and we didn't play our you know, week after week we need to find ways to be able to come out victorious and we didn't do that and there's little small things still that we have to fix obviously and it's just another week of trying to get better and getting all these things fixed because it they hurt and it stings. Me able to go against a division team and not come out victorious and we know the weight of these games. So we have to do more. Like I said, I'll say all week we got to do more. >> Allowing that many points to them in the second half, that gave them life, that brought them back in it. What shifted from a defensive standpoint you guys were not able to be as effective as you were early? >> Um I wouldn't say we didn't I think just execution, the leaky yards. you know, some passes going for more than we wanted it to then runs getting little more leaky yards. There wasn't a bunch of big plays but it was just little small things that added up, let them get field goals and those points add up after a while then obviously the touchdown and just being able to we got to make more plays. I think we need to get more turnovers. It's something we've been emphasizing and talking about all week but we have to do do a better job of doing it actually making it happen. >> You've placed such heavy emphasis and earlier in the week when we talked to you about execution. Where was execution lacking? >> Um I thought it was really good. I have to go back and watch the tape. It didn't feel like we were coming off the sideline there was any big time like fixes as far as like people missing their assignments. I think it's just doing a little, you know, making making more plays, going outside of doing your assignment but making those plays when they come to each of us and just like I said leaky yards and little small things that just add up and then those turn into field goals, those three points end up turning Well, I think they only scored one touchdown, but a lot of field goals, that adds up to a good amount of points. So, uh we have to do more. >> What's the frustration level when you get the takeaway and it seems like that you guys are going to be able to stack some momentum and then it just goes the opposite direction? >> Yeah, it's always frustrating um when um when you're not when you're not able to build off of momentum. Uh forget everything I did myself at getting the turnover. If we got to do more as a team and as a defense and me as a as a person on this defense trying to lead, we have to make more splash plays. If I got one and it didn't lead to momentum, okay, I need to make another one. I need to find a way to get the ball out and just, you know, do more things to try and help my team and um getting one interception, yeah, it's cool, but there the ball was in the air a lot more and I feel like there's other opportunities that we could have got it and I think that could have built more momentum. So, I think um you know, we always want when we make plays, you have to capitalize and use that momentum because momentum is a great thing in football, so we got >> What's the sentiment in the locker room right now? >> Um I mean, we're not down on ourselves, but obviously really disappointed, but the message is just what are we going to do about it? We're going to keep going. We can't sit down and, you know, just sit in our sorrow right now. It's like no matter what, the process stays the same. If we won, we're back in the building tomorrow to work hard and fix our mistakes. We lose, obviously it hurts a lot more and it's we hate losing, but the same process, we're going to be back in the building tomorrow to fix those same mistakes, but um obviously the urgency after losing is times 10 more than anything just as men and as, you know, competitors. So, we I think just the whole thing of this whole interview, we got to do more. >> What's going through your head when you hear the boos out there? >> I don't hear it. Uh we're not you know, I'm not driven, me personally, off of what the crowd is thinking about us. Obviously, they're we're just as frustrated as them, um but I think uh we just got to we got to give them a reason to not boo us. Um I think um the product that we put on the field, they're going to do what they want. They're they're fans and if they're not happy with the product that we're doing, we have to be better. I take ownership of that and obviously we want our fans to come in this building and be happy and leave happy walking out this building and so do we. Trust me, we want to win more than anybody in this world, but we have to do it. >> What's the biggest thing that needs to change? >> Learn how to stop losing, I think. As corny as that sounds, we have to figure out the things that were that are making us lose and stop doing those things and then then then winning will be a habit. >> What things do you look at Keenan and say this is what we got to stop doing? >> Um I think just the phrase bad ball. I think there's a lot of things that are showing up that we just just minimize. Just controllable things and just being able to create more plays. I think that's the one thing we got to just like take it up on ourselves to you know, find find a ball, get the ball. PBU's need to turn into tip balls, overthrows like I got today. Like that I need to do that more often, being in position to get those and like everybody just look at yourself and be like how can I make a play to help this team win? >> Keenan, how would you put in words what happened out there today? >> Uh disappointed for sure. Um feel like we came out second half and just damn near laid eggs, like literally. >> The How do you guys prevent this from spiraling? Obviously two and four things aren't going well. How do you I guess sort of correct this? >> I just get back to work. It's really all it is to do. Get back to work, look at the film, see what we can correct. Go internally, you know. Focus on yourself first and then collectively come out together and put it back out there. >> What's the biggest issue that you think is missing right now? >> Uh probably just execution. Um I feel like I feel like the plays are out there. We're just not getting it done. >> To hear the boos, what goes through your head? >> Tough. Tough. >> What was your takeaway from coach's message after the game? >> Uh right on cue. Um can't you can't turn the ball over in this league. Uh especially in the red zone. You know, it's just hard to come back from that. And then um punt punt returns um or punt punt block and the kick return, you know, at the end uh you know, it's tough to win like those. >> What did you tell Daniel after this game? Obviously, a few overthrows, couple some turnovers. >> haven't talked to him. >> What would you say to him? >> Uh just keep your head up. Um you know, next play next play mentality. you know, he's been in this league a long time, so you know, he knows um how it goes. And I'm staying up there. Got to get right back to it and um come back next week ready to go. >> You guys have played football a long time. I guess how do you keep moments like this from rolling or unraveling further? >> Yeah, I think that's the main thing. Don't let games like this, you know, define who you are. Um it's obviously a game that you want to win. And um you know, felt like we had a we had a good shot at it. Um but uh don't don't let it define you. But we got to clean up the turnovers for sure. >> What quarterback hit for you guys in the past 12 or 13? What have you seen that's been coming? >> Yeah, we got to get pressure on the quarterback. And we got to protect too as well. And I'm going to go back and look at that tape really hard. >> How would you evaluate Daniel so far this season? I know you said you love him, but the performance has not been quite frankly good. >> Yeah, you know, I think he knows he's got to play better. I got to coach better. There's a lot of things. It's not on one guy. But we got to do a lot of things better. >> Shame, do you have the talent to win? >> I believe we do. >> So to be clear, is he your starting quarterback moving >> Yes, he's our starting quarterback. >> Obviously this a low win. How do you keep this from spiraling out of control further? >> I think the biggest thing is you can't quit in this league. You don't quit on anything. We're two and four right now. We got a huge game coming up. We got a lot to fix in a hurry, um, to get ready to go for Minnesota. >> Why do you think you guys had so much trouble with the blitz today? >> Um, I think they did some good things. Why do you still believe in him after what we're seeing? >> Well, I think the preparation and how much he cares about the game, um, goes a long way with me. >> Were you seeing this type of performance at all throughout the week? >> Not at all. Um, our guys felt good. Felt like the preparation good, but clearly not good enough. Um, so we got to look at our process this week. >> How would you describe your tone to the team? >> About the same as I'm with you guys right now. Um, I think, uh, just overall didn't execute well enough in some situations. Um, I think obviously taking care of the ball is critical uh, to sustaining those drives and finishing with points. Um, so I've got to do a better job with that. And, yeah, overall we got to execute better. >> When you look at at the turnovers back on film throughout the season, is there any commonality in them? Like, are you trying to make something out of nothing when it's not there? Or is there anything you're seeing? >> Yeah, I there's sometimes if I force some stuff that's not there and and I got to be smart about that and know when know when it's there and know when it's not and when to when to lay the ball off. >> What did you see on the second interception? >> Yeah, I just uh Yeah, I thought I could get it in there. I couldn't. I got to lay the ball off. >> How would you describe your level of play this season? >> Um I I don't think it's been consistent enough. I think um certainly today wasn't consistent enough. I thought we did some good things offensively. We moved the ball well and then some bad stuff and and and yeah, not consistent enough. >> Why are the most you've been hit all season? What did you see up front with the protection today? >> Um yeah, I don't know. I'll go back and look at the tape and see where where I could have done a better job getting the ball in my hands. >> Daniel, what do you what do you feel like you need to clean up I guess overall throughout the first six weeks of the season? >> Yeah, I think taking care of the ball for one I think is the obvious one. I think go back and and see what it looks like, but you know, I got to do a better job diagnosing it and getting the ball out of my hands. >> Daniel, obviously fans have a strong reaction when they're not happy. I'm sure you've heard it. How do you process that? >> Yeah, I mean I think we didn't play well enough today. We got to play better and and um give them something to cheer about. So, um I understand that and and that's on us to to play better. >> Daniel, after the two scores that happened in the field, any complacency coming out of halftime? >> Uh no, I think we just we just didn't execute well enough in the second half and that third quarter. Everybody um understanding where we came up short and where uh where we can be better, where we can improve as a group. Um, taking accountability for the mistakes uh we've made and then uh making sure that they're fixed. Um, so I think that's what's critical now. Thank you. >> I mean that it hurts. That that one hurts. It it stings. You know, you don't want you don't want to lose division games at home. That's just something that you don't want to do. So, it's on us. No one's coming to save us, but it you got to look yourself in the mirror and then figure out what type of team that you that you want to be. And you want to be a really good team, you just can't lose division games at home. >> Between the interceptions and fumbles, how devastating were the turnovers like >> That's that's number one. Obviously, turnovers play a big factor in the game. You know, myself included. I mean, you you got to ensure that that ball's 100% secured and protected all the way to the ground. And anytime you it's almost like shooting yourself in the foot. Like those are some things that you can't control. It's going to be hard to win in this league whether it's a division opponent, non-division opponent, it's going to be hard to to win this league. So, that's number one. I mean, we got to we got to stop shooting ourselves in the foot. >> This was a division game, but I [clears throat] mean, you you guys were pretty heavily favored in this one. How do you keep like over the next week or so, how do you keep things from really getting out of control? >> I think understanding, like I mentioned, no one's coming to save us. And it doesn't matter about who's favored or who's not or who's expected to win. It's what did you do throughout the week? Did you prepare the right way? And then ultimately on Sunday, did you execute and did you put on display what you practiced all week? Cuz that's what matters. It's about It's about results. It's about going through that process throughout the week so that when Sunday comes, you get the results that you >> JP, there were boos. There were chance of fire valor. What was going through your head when you heard all that from the fans? >> I wasn't even listening to the the fans at that point. I mean, you're locked into the game. You're trying to figure out what can we do to ex- score one more point uh than the opponent. But I mean, but you're saying that I mean, that you never want to hear that from your home crowd. I mean, you know, that doesn't feel good whatsoever. You know, you never want your crowd booing you. You know, you're the home team. You never want that. >> Jonathan, on the outside, there are a lot of questions about obviously the guys in this locker room whether you can get it done. Do you believe you can and why? >> I I do believe we can get it done and like I mentioned, you you you see it throughout the week at practice and it's executed to a T and you feel really good about the plan. But then when Sunday comes, it's no matter what they show us. Everyone does scouting. Everyone does their research. Everyone plans. Whatever they throw at you, can you find a way to still execute that job? Now, obviously, if there are adjustments that need to be made because, you know, it's not advantageous for us, we'll make those. But then even when you make those adjustments, you still have to execute and you have to make those critical plays. But then you also, like I mentioned, you can't shoot yourself in the foot whether it's turnovers, uh procedural penalties. Like a lot of those things already put you behind for the play >> starts. >> JT, fire valor
