title: Saints vs. Giants Postgame Show | 2026 NFL Week 6
text: Touchdown Saints. >> Welcome in to the Saints postgame show presented by Uber Eats. Kalia Butler, Gus Katenuel here with you. We'll be joined by Scott Shanley here in a second, but it's a story of survival here, Gus. The Saints survive 34-27 against the Giants. And we saw that final quarter. Let's talk about that a little bit because that's when people started to get a little bit nervous here. Able to survive, make some plays, saw something different with the quarterbacks when it came to the Giants, but the end of the day, it came down to surviving that final quarter. Yeah, this is why you literally wait till the game ends because we had at least three quarters worth of something completely different we're going to discuss and talk about and we still will because at the end of the day the Saints do win 3427 and they did earn that win and in the manner they did it. We have a lot to get into. That said, a lot of people are going to discuss and see. Hey, 10 minutes and uh 22 seconds left in the fourth quarter. You're up 34-10. The starters come out of the game two plays into the backups coming in. Spencer Rattler hands it off to CJ Donaldson. There's that turnover or fumble and that somehow sparks life into the Giants and all of a sudden you're hoping that a fourth and one pass in the end zone goes incomplete with time expiring for you to win cuz that's what happened for the Saints to get the win. So don't like how that happened there at the end of the fourth quarter and that's something I'm looking forward to seeing what coach Kelly Moore has to say about that. But man, what what a snowball effect because the Saints did the same thing, Kalia. 34 unanswered points in this game. Took a 10- nothing deficit into a 3410 Saints lead, which was as incredible as what we saw in the fourth quarter. But bottom line, needed that win, but you got one >> as you mentioned. And towards the beginning of the game, like you said, you weren't sure what it was going to look like. You have another first quarter that's looking a little bit tough. The slow starts kind of starting to pile up, but then you get into that second quarter. You're able to score right before things get a little murky for you. You go in, you tie things up at the half, and then you have 24 consecutive points as you mentioned. But let's take a look at how we got to those 24 consecutive points. Let's roll the highlights here really quick because defense came up quickly for this team once again having some big plays. You have Cam Jordan who had his TL in this one. People love seeing Cam Jordan make big plays. >> Yeah, no doubt. Look, he's been saying it the last couple of weeks, too. He wants to kind of get looking and playing a little bit like he did last season where he had 10 sacks and it was nice to be able to see him active. He had two tackles. You mentioned the tackle for loss, but he was active today and that was fun. >> Yeah. Then we had a Carl Granderson who had three and a half sacks in the last two games. One there, then you had Chase Young's tackle for loss. Then you have Pete Warner who got involved in the sack party as well. Yeah, no doubt. Pete Warner you were talking about. He has 10 tackles, four solo, a sack, a tackle for loss as well. He and so many defensive players. He had to keep scrolling to find all of the different players. >> Let's take a look at that fumble recovery as you saw by Oscar Delta helped set up the touchdown here. And then we go for the run. You have Tyler using his legs a little bit, which we love to see and he's gotten more comfortable doing so. But then we set up the touchdown, which we kind of mentioned here. You're taking a look. Tyler back there and then you make a connection right when you need it. You start scoring. Bryce uh Lance had his first career touchdown in today's game. >> And then of course here's the history making touchdown reception. Alvin Chimera looking like the old school AK-41 there. A catch and go making himself part of a very special club. >> Yeah, we'll be able to highlight him a little bit later. As you mentioned, made history. No surprise there. Then you have Tyler Shuck who had his rushing touchdown. But let's look at the defense one more time because Martin Emerson Jr. had an absolute day. That was his first reception just in today's game. Then you have defense coming up one more time cuz you have Julian Blackman who's been involved in being able to get some interceptions a couple of times this season and that helps just set up another touchdown for the Saints. Take a look here. You have Tyler Shuck who has the connection with Chris Ave. Chris Ave just living up to who he is. We we talk about the contract, we talk about the extension, just what that looked like, making big plays when you needed him to most. But I wanted to highlight Tyler Shuck a little bit here. Uh just the kind of recovery that he had from this last game compared to now. Obviously, last game against Minnesota was a little bit of a tougher one for him in terms of the passing yards. Uh you take a look at how he's maintaining the ability to take control of games and staying poised is what stands out most. >> Yeah. And I think when you look also at this game too, let's not forget Jeremiah Wright going out of coming in because Caesar goes out with a knee injury. And that's something that again that offensive line has had to, you know, alternate different bodies. You already have a starting left tackle that's different for a while. And look, let's be honest. I think one of the things that may not get mentioned just because of the 34 straight points by the Saints and the, you know, 17 straight points by the Giants. But the run game today, we can highlight in a little bit here as well. lots of backs helping out and that's going to help your quarterback because when you look at the stats Kalia 16 of 30 144 yards is not anything you're gonna you know write home about or anything of that nature but the three TDs and more importantly zero interceptions and I think when you highlight that touchdown catch you talk about with the l >> that's that connection they have he's thrown to that front pylon he's throwing to a spot Chris knew to get there Tyler threw that ball before anyone was really open there and he was able to get that >> and it's the ability to get get it into those tight windows. That has kind of been a highlight. Uh you see the continued chemistry that is kind of starting to build uh between Tyler Shuck here and his receivers. Let's join in now with Scott Shanley who I'm sure has plenty to talk about when it comes to the defensive front of things. Scott, I'm sure you liked what this defense was capable of doing. You have Jamus Winston who we kind of talked about the ability to maybe run into a couple sacks. They were able to set the tone early. They definitely didn't. I think you saw the game swung in the middle of that game when the defense stepped up, started taking the football away. And anytime you're plus three in the turnover takeaway battle, offense took care of the ball. Defense took away the football as well as special teams. So, anytime you're plus three, you're going to win a lot of football games. Um, so much good. The defense applied pressure. They made the plays. We we said going into this game, Jameus was going to throw you some. He's always been kind of a gunslinger. You made him pay when he threw those. And then late in the game, uh, McCarthy came in and just threw up some balls. But I think defensively, you're excited about what you were able to do. You were able to take control of that game, except in the fourth quarter where really your only job as a defense is just to keep the ball in front of you and there were just too many chunk plays late in the game that kind of kept the Giants in it. >> Yeah, I like what you mentioned there in terms of just keeping everything in front of them. That's what we saw for a majority of these first three quarters. in the fourth quarter, I would assume that, you know, some tiresome legs start to come involved, uh, trying to just keep them ahead of you. What did you see the Saints do defensively that maybe shifted in the fourth quarter, but the ability to still get it done and just keep it where you get a win? >> Yeah, I think obviously you don't want to go into the entire fourth quarter and say, "We're just going to play prevent defense. We're going to stack everybody 30 yards deep and make them check it down." There's logic to that, but at the same time, you still want to play normal football and not just give them 15 yards because they'll still metriculate the ball down a field that way, too. So, I think defensively, you you play what you do, but be cognizant of the game situation. The only way they can hurt you is going deep. And I'll be honest, JJ McCarthy threw up a lot of wild Hail Mary balls, and it was just truly one-on-one plays, and their receivers made the plays and brought them down. I think if you're a defensive back, those are the 50/50 balls that you have to make some of those. What about the response there? What did you like about that, Scott? Because, as you mentioned, you start with a Jameus Winston in the game. You kind of maybe know what to expect, but then you have JJ McCarthy who steps in and has 243 yards, three scoring drives. How did the defense respond to that? And again, just being able to keep them comfortable enough where they still had that seven-point lead. Yeah, I think the one thing you learn as a player in this league is that you can never be comfortable until there are zero zero up on that clock because even up 24 points, wild things happen. Um, utilizing the timeouts, getting free and outs, things like that, and right away the their offense has the ball back. So, unfortunately, this was a game where you you feel like as a player and a coach, finally we we kind of get everybody off our back. We played great. We're going to dominate a three in one NFC East leading team. But just like that, things things can change. That's what makes the NFL so great is the the elite players and the coaches and every single play matters and how you manage the game goes a long way. But um you we always say just the Giants are paid to make plays too and they made more plays in the fourth quarter to get them back in the game. But for the other three quarters, the Saints were the better team and and that ended up being the W. And that's that's the that's the goal every single week. And this is the business of winning. >> I like I like that. This is the business of winning. Let's get into some specific players as well. You have Martin Everson Jr. who comes in has a very significant impact. Uh his ability to just be able to play in coverage. You have that Malik Neighbors uh who obviously having a fantastic day here of his own, but again the ability to try to contain him as much as possible. What did you like from that Scott? What did you see from Martin Emerson Jr. today? I mean, making plays and anytime you have a DB who makes plays on the ball and is a ball disruptor and and that's what you do. I mean, you're you're paid to go out there and cover guys and it wasn't an easy matchup. You mentioned it going into this week. Malik Neighbors is an outstanding player. He's a true number one in this league and uh Emerson rose to that challenge. He he he loved that challenge, went out there, played great, and he made the plays when the ball was thrown his way. And and also Emerson's a great story. You know, Torres Achilles battled back from that injury and now he's, you know, player of the game today defensively taking the football away and giving your offense uh extra possessions. >> What did you like about the pressure that we saw the Saints applying today as well? We've seen it in the last couple of games in terms of applying some pressure to the quarterback. Obviously, we saw the transition in this game as well. What is that continued front able to do? >> I think they're just being very active. I I think Christian Boyd, we talked about him last week. He's taking advantage of his snaps. He's playing really good at defensive tackle right now. But also, you look at what coach Daly is doing defensively. Getting Carl Granderson back has been has been huge. They really missed him when he was out um with an injury. So, I like what Coach Daly is doing. Putting Granderson and Chase Young on the same side. You really put offensive lines into binds. When you put two really good rushers on one side of the ball, all the attention goes that way. Now, you have one-on- ones on the backside and guys are winning and collapsing the pocket. And I think that was really the story of the game. you were pushing guys into the lap of of Jameus Winston early in this game. He was panicking and throwing up some balls. So rush and coverage go hand in hand and I thought you saw a really good rush with really good coverage and that's why you saw so many turnovers. >> Let's take a look at the offensive side with you as well, Scott, because someone that you know pretty well, Drew Brees, who was on the call at halftime, he said he wants to see tempo, aggression, and some play action calls involved. And in that second half, that's kind of exactly what we saw. How was that able to help the Saints get to a victory today? >> Yeah, play action football, and I know a lot of people talked about this this week, what Drew mentioned it last week on the telecast, is as a as a linebacker, I love playing against offenses who are in the shotgun primarily. You can see the ball, the quarterback doesn't turn his back to you. When you get play action teams, it's really hard to play linebacker because you don't know where the football is at all times. Does the running back have it? Is the quarterback pulling it? It creates hesitation defensively. So just adding there's more play action in in today's package and then running the football better. I thought Pre Miller did an outstanding job. Jeremiah Wright was outstanding. He went in for for Caesar Ruiz when Caesar went out with the injury. So there were a couple series there in the game that really changed the flow of the game. They changed the entire tempo and it all started with being able to run the football and that opened up the play action passing game. What was different about this game, Scott, in terms of we kind of saw a common trend of having a slow start, but again, we saw that pickup before the end of the half, I guess. How important was it to have that momentum swing before the half ended? >> Oh, right before the half, what really I think was what was the difference in the game? I I know the game got out of control in the third quarter, 24 to 10, but that series before the half when it was 10 to nothing, Saints go down and get a score, they kick off, and then they get a takeaway right away again. And they scored, I believe, 10 seconds and 70 seconds. That to me determined the outcome of the game, more so than than a lot that happened in the second half. And there was a lot that happened in the second half. But you go into the locker room tie game when you feel like we haven't played well and it's zero to zero, that does everything to the confidence of a team. And I think that's why you saw the Saints with a bounce in their step in the third quarter. They played some of their best football. They reminded me of that team that was in Baltimore a few weeks ago. So that sequence of 77 seconds before the half, I think was the determining factor in the game. >> Scott, I got to know, how are you feeling about these away environments in particular, it seems like the team is maybe showing up the most when they're on the road. Do they do they like playing in this sort of more hostile environment to get the job done? What What are you seeing from that front? I jokingly said, "I foresee you playing Baltimore, New York. Let's just play all the games in the Northeast or we'll just lie to them and tell them we're in the Northeast. We move the dome." But they played some really good football. And uh you know, I think there's a little bit of truth. And this is not that you don't like playing at home, but sometimes there's extra distractions at home. You have family coming in, you have people that want tickets, you have all these things. And sometimes when you go on the road, there's kind of a bunker down mentality. You go, you're away, you're isolated. And this team has played some good football. Baltimore and New York and uh this team just needed some confidence back after what happened with the the Vikings game and the Falcons game and all the outside noise. They needed a game like this where they proved to themselves that they are closer to that Baltimore team than they are closer to the Atlanta and Minnesota team. >> Let's bring Gus back into this as well because Gus has been jotting down a lot of notes here. Gus, what just stands out to you? Maybe a specific stat that you liked most about this win today. Yeah, I think Scott would like this, too. 22 defensive players had at least one tackle in this game. I mean, I mean, obviously, when you have the week and the consecutive losses like you're having right now, you need to step up. And the way you step up is what can you do individually? And I think that's what stands out to me. When 22 players have at least a tackle, have something in the box score, that tells me that they're doing their part. What can you do? You hear that phrase all the time, Kalia, you're one of 11, you know, you won 11th of the job, but 22 defensive players getting at least one tackle and then five sacks and you're getting it from everybody. And then you get the interceptions from Emerson and look, he comes in cuz Kool-Aid wasn't feeling well apparently per reports online. So you have Wright step in because of an injury. You have Emerson come in cuz Koul's not feeling well under the weather. Those guys provided, you know, an opportunity for you to win. They did something for you. So, I think that's something that stands out cuz if you want to turn things around, you want to show you're a good football team, then you have to step up, right? I mean, you you always hear that phrase looking in the mirror and all that stuff, but when you look in a mirror, what are you going to do? I mean, I I love I know you're going to do what you're going to do, Cleo, but what can I do, you know, to help that? So, >> it's going to be the next man up sort of mentality. That's something that head coach Kell Moore has talked about a lot. Obviously, just a common theme throughout sports in general is who's going to step up and make plays when the person in front of you is down and the depth has kind of spoke today? Maybe that has been in question at certain times before, but what stands out to you about the depth that this team does have and how that showed up today? >> Yeah, that I mean, look, take a look at the the second thing that really stood out that you guys were just talking about and that's the run game, right? I mean, we how how many weeks have we talked about the run game and needing to stop the run, more importantly, getting it to go? And again, the numbers aren't going to stare right at you and go, you did not have a 100yard rusher. I get it. But the backs combined for 143 yards, and you add Tyler Shucks 32, 175 yards came on the ground. That helps, right? All that little bit. >> Um, you had Miller with 20 carries for 70 yards. CJ Donaldson 6 yards, 39, Alvin put in seven with for 34. So, it was spread around. So, you had a bunch of backs helping out. Goes to your depth question there. And it helps your quarterback, you know. So, I I I just think it's you hear it, it's not a sexy phrase, but complimentary football. And that's what that was a thing today. >> I want to invite Scott back in here really quick because as you mentioned, the run game was a big part that wanted to be implemented early, was implemented in this game, probably the most that we have seen. And I think that was the difference in the game, especially the third quarter. you started to move their defensive line. And when you start to move a defensive line, you're pushing guys into the linebacker's laps. The defensive coordinator gets nervous. Now, we need to start bringing pressure. When you bring pressure, that's less guys in coverage. So, to me, everything revolves around the running game and and how you establish it and how you get it going, especially early in the game. What about defending the run as well? Because we didn't necessarily see that from the Giants as much today, especially comparison to teams that the Saints have played before, but there's an expectation that Cam Scatteraboo is going to get involved pretty early on. You didn't really see him get many touches. Is that credit to something that the Saints were doing defensively on that front too in defending the run? Yeah, I thought the Giants, in my honest opinion, I think the Giants didn't fit enough to run the game, especially early on. But when you have Isaiah likely and you have Malik Neighbor, you get spoiled again. You want to get the ball into their hands instead of turning around and handing the football off. Scatters in the doghouse with all the fumbles recently, so they were kind of going by of a committee approach. text: Well, then why don't we guess who is not going 17-0? Guess who will be nowhere near a perfect season. Alth although we already knew that entering today. Or how about we guess who's in last place in the NFC West? That's right. It is your super team. Everybody's favorite super team, the Los Angeles Rams. They lost the Australian market to begin this season by deciding that jetlag didn't matter to them, that they could just waltz into Melbourne and win a football game against the best team in the NFL in week one. That didn't go well for the Rams. They got blown out by the 49ers. They lost to the Denver Broncos and Bone Knicks, who's not a very good quarterback, not a good quarterback at all. They found a way to today lose to the Arizona Cardinals. Jacobe Brassette and the Arizona Cardinals beat the Rams on the road and LA is now two and four. An absolute embarrassment in LA. An embarrassment to the media especially that has continued saying that the Rams are some kind of Super Bowl favorites. I heard so much over the course of this week that the Rams somehow because they had a yardage advantage over some of their opponents that they were some kind of sleeping giant that was going to turn this around. And anybody who seriously analyzes football will tell you that yardage is without context probably the most overrated statistic that there is. We've have so many more sophisticated ways of measuring who's good and who's not in the National Football League. So, if you're looking at raw yardage, you might as well be analyzing football in 1976, not in 2026. The Rams by EPA per play by DVOA. This was at best a slightly above average football team because the special teams had been such a disaster. And it continued being a disaster today as the Rams lost to the Cardinals. But at best, if you actually looked at the tape and you looked at the metrics, the Rams weren't weren't good. And we expected it to be close against the Arizona Cardinals, who also aren't good. I think the Rams surprised even me today with their ineptitude. Entering the final drive of the game, the Rams had 170 yards of total offense against an defense that ranked number 29. You guys saw how much Brock Birdie carved up the Arizona Cardinals. You've seen how many teams have carved up the Arizona Cardinals. Stafford, Nakua, McVey, and the Rams and all those tight ends. They couldn't even pick up fourth and one when they're trying to hand off to backup tight end playing fullback. I mean, this was this was on another level of embarrassment for LA and they dropped to two and four. They are now officially in last place in NFC West and it is time for the Rams to not mathematically face elimination, but their backs are up completely against the wall at this point. They're going to have to rip off several consecutive victories. Everybody was talking about the schedule being softer for the Rams leaving last week's loss against the Buffalo Bills. I, you know, we mentioned that on on Monday night, but Mike is saying, is it Tai Simpson time in LA? I don't think it's that time yet because they've the Rams have invested so much in this season. We saw it in Australia when they decided that they didn't need to fly to Australia of all places until the day before the football game. And hey, respect to them for operating with conviction when they decided to fly to Australia the day before the game. But it it to me it's it it's staggering to for all that we have sat through being lectured by the media over the course of the off season that no Matthew Stafford this, Shawn McVey that, they know better than you. This team is going to go undefeated. If you don't think so, you don't know football. to predict the Rams to to be the winner of this division, I think, was a was a very casual prediction, we could put it that way. It is just staggering to see a team not actually address what is wrong with it and just continue to circle down the toilet as we've seen from the Rams this year. title: Jordan Love says ‘CONFIDENCE IS THROUGH THE ROOF’ after Packers’ win vs. Cowboys | SC with SVP
text: It's a pleasure to welcome back to the program the quarterback of the Green Bay Packers, Jordan Love, after a 10-point victory over the Dallas Cowboys. Jordan, thank you for waiting in the tunnel for us to come out of this commercial break. And forgive me for what I'm about to do. Um, obviously in that game, we didn't do that. There's a lot of stuff we looked at um made some changes at figured out what we needed to do better and uh we've been playing a lot better since then and it's just about taking it one week at a time building on the things that we do well and uh trying to clean up our process. But uh we played a lot better than that game for sure tonight >> clearly and you did last week with your rival Chicago in town and now you've got another rival up in Detroit next week. There was a great stat on the broadcast tonight about the Golden Watson duo. And, um, you know, the guys we got at receiver, they're very capable of, uh, getting behind DBs and, uh, making plays down the field. So, I love it. And obviously, we got to go out there and make those plays when they're called. And we did that last week. And uh we had some plays tonight uh that we did the same thing. So we just got to keep building. Like that's that's a gigantic tell in the National Football League to me. How how critical is that for you when you look at a box score after a night? Is that the line your eyes is drawn to? Oh man, of course. Uh that's that's where you win and lose the game right there. You got to find a way as offense to to execute third down, stay on the field, convert, and uh come away with points. And I think that's an area that uh we we've had to look at and clean up and get better at and improve at. And we've done that early on. It wasn't where we needed to be. And I think we're we're making strides, but there's still a lot out there for us. But man, third downs, that's the money down. You got to find ways to to extend those drives and uh convert third downs. >> Yeah. I I think people probably get sick of me saying the money down because that's what it is. All right, let me close with this. I mentioned Detroit's up next and you you just look, Chicago and Dallas, big gigantic games. Everybody's watching. Um and it's important to stay present, but we know it appears at some point you'll get some help in the back field. We don't know when Jacobs will be back, but perhaps that soon. And at some point number one's going to be back. So you're talking about two giant difference makers on each side of the ball. When you think about what you guys might look like that, how enticing is it to consider? >> Oh, it's it's very enticing. Like you said, you know, you you get two uh difference makers for for our team, get them coming back. Um and it it'll definitely play a huge role in that. But like you mentioned, you know, we got a NFC North uh team next week and you know, we got to be able to handle business. That's a very good team. We see them all the time. So, um, we got to we got to attack this week, get better, and, uh, find a way to go play our best game next week. >> All right. Thanks for your patience tonight. Thanks for throwing the headset on, man. Be well until our pass cross. Good luck, good health, most importantly. Thank you. >> Yes, sir. I'll see you. >> All right. Look forward to it. You see the Packers and the Cowboys. You're talking about legendary franchises with some history. Packers haven't lost to the Cowboys since in the regular season, I should say, since n uh 2016. And it's a seven-game unbeaten streak now. The longest against Dallas all time. Previous longest streak when they beat the Cowboys in the first six ever matchups between the two teams in the 60s under the toutelage of a gentleman by the name of Vince Lombardi.
